prompt: A pendulum returns to its starting position whenever $\cos\theta = 1$. What is the general solution of $\cos\theta = 1$?
hint: Cosine reaches its maximum of $1$ only at the very right of the unit circle.

hints.text: Cosine reaches its maximum of $1$ only at the very right of the unit circle.
That happens once per full turn, so the solutions are spaced $360^\circ$ apart.

explanation: $\cos\theta = 1$ only at the point $(1, 0)$ on the unit circle, which is angle $0^\circ$.
Every full revolution returns to that same point, and a full revolution is $360^\circ$.
So the general solution is $\theta = 360^\circ k$ for any integer $k$ — the pendulum comes home once per complete swing cycle.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why $180^\circ k$ is wrong
steps: Choice B would include $\theta = 180^\circ$, but $\cos 180^\circ = -1$, not $1$.
That is the pendulum at the far end of its swing, the opposite of where it started.
Maximum values repeat once per period, so the spacing is a full $360^\circ$.
